The issue has sparked debate online, with some calling for Kenya to introduce retaliatory measures against Nigerian passport holders to ensure fairness.
One Nigerian academic weighed in, suggesting that Kenya should impose reciprocal visa restrictions to push Nigeria into reviewing its current stance.
The dispute comes against the backdrop of Kenya’s recent move to ease travel across the continent by scrapping Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) requirements for most African countries.
The policy, implemented in July last year, allows citizens from nearly all African states, except a few flagged over security concerns, to enter Kenya without prior authorisation.
Under the framework, Nigerians are among African nationals permitted to travel to Kenya visa-free and can even extend their stay, a privilege now at the centre of the diplomatic backlash.
